Calculate parity- and age-adjusted total fertility rates

Source: R/calculate_patfr.R
calculate_patfr.Rd

Progress a synthetic cohort from parity zero through conditional age/parity fertility schedules using the HFD period fertility-table midpoint convention. Women in the final open parity band remain there and can have repeated births. This is a deterministic fertility table without mortality or explicit birth spacing, not a microsimulation or an exact continuous-time hazard solution.

Usage

calculate_patfr(rates)

Arguments

rates

A fertility process or a table with age_start, age_end, parity_start, parity_end and rate or rate_fertility in births per woman-year at that current parity. Optional time_start, time_end, group, union_type and legacy union_status define separate strata.

Value

A tibble with the supplied stratification columns, finite age_start, age_end, and patfr. Empty results retain their column types. A supplied unassigned_births attribute is preserved.

Details

Separate the same period, group and union-type strata as calculate_tfr(); select female rows when sex is present. Parity itself is integrated over. Each stratum has its own cohort: a union-type-specific index assumes that type throughout, without partnership or group transitions. Every age must have complete, nonoverlapping parity coverage from zero to one open final category. Finite parity bounds must be nonnegative integers. Each parity must cover the same contiguous finite age range. Missing included rates yield NA for that stratum. No missing-rate zero fill is performed here.

Upper-open age rows are omitted, warning on known nonzero omitted female rates. The returned finite age range defines the calculation: all women start at parity zero at its lower bound. Split at integer ages and input boundaries into steps of at most one year. On each step of length d, use progression probability d*m / (1 + d*m/2) and midpoint entry/exit exposure, following HFD Methods Protocol (2015), sections 8.3-8.4. Probabilities above one are rejected. Fractional steps generalize the annual convention. HFD endpoint mapping and missing-cell choices can change agreement with its published indices. See https://www.humanfertility.org/File/GetDocumentFree/Docs/methods.pdf.
